newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico has to reduce inflation more - Fin Ministy.
newsitem.headline: Mexico has to reduce inflation more - Fin Ministy.

text.p: Mexico's inflation target of 15 percent for 1997 is not a floor for reducing inflation, Deputy Finance Minister Martin Werner told analysts in a conference call on Wednesday.
When asked if the government would try to have inflation continue to fall or if it was nearing a floor, Werner said, "We don't think this is a floor. We are going to reduce inflation significantly.

"The central bank is committed and its objective is to reduce the rate of inflation. So we are not saying that the inflation rate that we expect or the one that the market expects for this year to be a floor in any sense," Werner said.

Mexico saw some price increases in widely-consumed goods, like milk and tortillas, right at the end of 1996 that fueled inflation at the start of 1997, but government officials said this does not mean that inflation for the year will be "misaligned."
